evidence.quote: State law requires that every person or entity doing business in the state of Nevada obtain a business license annually. The State Business License Fee is $500 for Corporations, and $200 for all other business types. The State Business License must be renewed annually.

The annual renewal fee is $500 for Corporations, and $200 for all other business entity types. The fee and renewal form are due on the last day of the anniversary month in which the license was originally filed.

For entities that are formed under NRS Title 7, the business license fee is due at the time an Initial List of Officers or Annual List of Officers is due. The State Business License Fee is in addition to the fees for the initial or annual list.

Yes. A single-member Limited Liability Company is an entity required to file an annual list with the Secretary of State and therefore, is also required to maintain a State Business License. An LLC's State Business License Application is now part of the LLC's Annual List of Managers/Members.

notes:
Two levies, one record, which is why the basis is hybrid, and this is the California shape with one difference that matters: the two halves belong to two agencies. The flat part is the State Business License, $200 a year for every entity type except a corporation, collected by the Secretary of State and owed by every person or entity doing business in Nevada. The scaled part is the Commerce Tax, collected by the Department of Taxation on Nevada gross revenue above $4,000,000 at rates that vary by industry. minimumAnnualUsd carries the floor; the scaled part is in the evidence and in this note, and it is not a separate record.
Nevada calls the flat levy a license. It is a recurring state-level charge for the privilege of doing business, owed annually for as long as the entity exists, and it passes the inclusion test on substance whatever the label says. filedWith names the Secretary of State because that is who collects the floor minimumAnnualUsd carries; the Commerce Tax half is the Department of Taxation, and the field cannot say both.
collectedWithAnnualReport is true, and it is a PARTIAL overlap rather than an equality. Root states.json carries annual_report_fee 350 for Nevada, which is the $150 annual list plus this $200 license on the same filing, so the $200 is already counted there and a total-cost consumer must not add it again. The 350 and the 200 are not the same number and are not meant to be. Commerce Tax is not in root's figure at all and must be added by any consumer whose reader exceeds the threshold.
firstYearExemption is false. A new Nevada LLC pays the license with its Initial List of Officers, due by the last day of the month after its organizational documents are filed, so the first year brings the payment forward rather than waiving it.
passThroughApplies is false on a direct constitutional prohibition rather than on an inference: article 10, section 1, subsection 9 of the Nevada Constitution forbids any income tax on the wages or personal income of natural persons, and a member's distributive share is personal income. The same subsection then expressly permits taxes on the income or revenue of a business, which is the constitutional room the Commerce Tax occupies and the reason a reader should not take "no income tax" to mean "nothing is levied here". The Department of Taxation's enumeration of the tax types it administers is kept as a second passage: it names no income tax of any kind, and it is what carries hasPTETElection, because an election into an entity-level income tax cannot exist where no such tax does.
PROVENANCE: the Secretary of State's FAQ was read in a browser on 2026-08-07 and its quotations are verified against a text snapshot taken the same day, because nvsos.gov serves an interstitial to every scripted client. That is a weaker guarantee than a live re-fetch and is recorded here so it is visible. It is no longer load-bearing: NRS 76.100 and 76.130 ground the $200, the due date and the annual-list tie from the statute itself, and the FAQ corroborates rather than carries.
needsReview: The Commerce Tax rate is not recorded. The Department of Taxation's page states that the rate varies by industry and publishes the per-NAICS-category table elsewhere, and none was read in this pass, so the record carries the $4,000,000 threshold and the revenue basis but no percentage. Reading that table would complete the scaled half of the regime. It does not touch minimumAnnualUsd, which is the flat license fee and is grounded in NRS 76.130.
